sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier differs from that of C. taquarussu in the larger head measurements in all respects, the darker and patchily coloured head capsule and the less distinct constriction; the nasus also differs between the two. Both worker sizes are larger than in C. taquarussu and the remaining characters are similar, differing only in the enteric valve (EVA): in this species the spines of both the anterior and the posterior rings of cushions are more robust, most conspicuously the longer spines at the caudal end (posterior margin).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Soldiers monomorphic. Head capsule yellow-brown, with pale patches on the posterior part and in the region between the constriction and the nasus, the nasus darkest. In dorsal view the posterior lobe of the head capsule is rounded, about 1.5 times as wide as the anterior lobe; the lateral margins of the anterior lobe are scarcely convex; the nasus is slender and cylindrical, tapering to a point in its apical tenth. Mandibles without an apical process. In lateral view the head capsule has two swellings, the upper one over the anterior lobe smaller and that over the posterior lobe larger; a pair of long setae arises from the middle of each lobe. The nasus bears about 60 short setae from its anterior third to the tip. In dorsal view the anterior margin of the pronotum is almost straight, the anterolateral margins semicircular, narrowing posteriorly into a narrow, incised posterior margin; the anterior margin has microscopic setae. Abdominal tergites with 8—12 long setae near the posterior margin and with many fine hairs scattered over the surface. Legs long, with scattered long setae and fine hairs. Antennae long, 15-segmented, the segment formula 2<3>4≥5. Measurements (n=10, mean (minimum—maximum)): head length 1.97 (1.90—2.04) mm, head length to the nasus base 1.14 (1.11—1.16) mm, nasus length 0.84 (0.79—0.90) mm, maximum head width 1.12 (1.09—1.16) mm, head width at the posterior margin of the antennal sockets 0.74 (0.72—0.77) mm, nasus width at midlength 0.09 (0.08—0.09) mm, head height at the occipital margin 0.79 (0.77—0.82) mm, pronotum width 0.59 (0.54—0.64) mm, hind tibia length 1.45 (1.38—1.53) mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The original does not give a separate description of characters, recording only that the alate of this species is essentially the same as described for C. taquarussu by Cuezzo et al. (2015a), with the same antennal segment formula 2<3>4≥5 and some measurements slightly larger. Measurements (male n=7/female n=2, mean (minimum—maximum)): head length to the postclypeus 0.94 (0.86—0.99)/1.03 (0.99—1.06) mm, head width including the compound eyes 1.26 (1.21—1.33)/1.33 (1.33) mm, compound eye diameter 0.35 (0.32—0.37)/0.36 (0.35—0.37) mm, ocellus diameter 0.11 (0.10—0.12)/0.14 (0.12—0.15) mm, distance from the compound eye to the ocellus 0.07 (0.05—0.09)/0.06 (0.05—0.07) mm, maximum pronotum width 1.04 (0.99—1.06)/1.20 (1.19—1.21) mm and median length 0.65 (0.62—0.69)/0.70 (0.69—0.72) mm, fore wing length (from the suture) 9.11 (8.91—9.41)/10.30 (10.20—10.40) mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Workers dimorphic. Head capsule pale red-brown, trapezoidal in dorsal outline; the dorsum bears 4 setae, 2 near the occiput and 2 farther forward. Antennae 15-segmented, the segment formula 2>3<4=5. Broad-gap major workers are commoner than narrow-gap minor workers. The enteric valve is the same in both sizes: it consists of a ring of 6 slender anterior cushions followed by a ring of 6 more robust posterior cushions; the anterior cushions bear about 5—16 pointed scales and the posterior cushions about 12—22 spines, the spines near the posterior margin (caudal end) distinctly longer. For the gut and mandibles see Cuezzo et al. (2015). Measurements (narrow-gap n=3/broad-gap n=10, mean (minimum—maximum)): head length to the postclypeus 0.69 (0.62—0.74)/0.80 (0.69—0.94) mm, head width 0.91 (0.89—0.94)/1.05 (0.99—1.14) mm, hind tibia length 1.14 (1.11—1.19)/1.34 (1.21—1.51) mm.

note: Adapted from the new-species description in Scheffrahn (2022), original in English; the alate section of the original only makes comparisons and does not describe characters separately; figure numbers (Figs 1—5), the holotype locality and type specimen records are not translated.
